results.title: Understanding Docker Image Tags: A Guide to Versions and Variants
results.content: # Understanding Docker Image Tags: A Guide to Versions and Variants. When working with Docker, you'll often encounter various image tags that help define the base image used for your containers. In this article, we’ll break down the different types of Docker image tags, their significance, and how to choose the right tag for your project. Common Docker Image Tags and Their Meanings. When pulling Docker images, you may notice tags like latest, alpine, or specific version names like bullseye or bookworm. Here's a breakdown of the most common Docker image tags:. This is perhaps the most commonly used Docker image tag. If no version is specified, Docker will pull the image with the latest tag by default. The slim tag represents a minimal version of the image, which has been stripped down to include only the core components necessary to run the application. Using Alpine as a base image can dramatically reduce the size of your Docker image while still providing all the essential components you need for your application. These tags specify a particular version of the software in the image. Sometimes, you'll see Docker images tagged with -testing, -stable, or -rc. The -minimal tag often refers to an image that contains only the essential packages and libraries needed to run an application, making it smaller and faster than its full version counterparts. Choosing the Right Docker Image Tag. The right Docker image tag depends on the specific needs of your application:. * For smaller images: Use tags like alpine or slim to reduce the size of your containers. * For compatibility with specific versions: Use versioned tags (e.g., node:14, python:3.9) to ensure you're using the exact version of the software your project needs. * lts (Long-Term Support): This tag indicates the image is based on a version of software with long-term support, providing extended security updates and bug fixes. Docker image tags are essential for specifying which base image your container will use. As Docker continues to evolve, keeping an eye on image tags will help you make more informed decisions about which images to use in your projects. * Running Ruby 4 with Ruby::BOX inside Docker (Alpine).

results.title: almalinux/8-base - Docker Image
results.content: ## almalinux/8-base. AlmaLinux OS 8 official base image. # almalinux/8-base repository overview. ### Quick reference. * `minimal`, `8-minimal`, `8.6-minimal`, `almalinux/8-minimal`⁠. ### Quick reference (cont.). official-images repo's `library/almalinux` label⁠. official-images repo's `library/almalinux` file⁠ (history⁠). docs repo's `almalinux/` directory⁠ (history⁠). ### AlmaLinux OS. #### About this image. AlmaLinux OS⁠ images can be use with all OCI complaint⁠ container runtime environments like Docker, Podman and Kubernetes and serve as drop-in replacemenets for `centos` images as it reaches End of Life⁠. ##### Platform image, `latest` tag. The default (platform) image is a general-purpose image with a full DNF stack and basic tools like bintools, find, tar, minimal-vim, etc. The `almalinux:latest` tag will always point to the latest stable release of the default image. `almalinux:8` or `almalinux:8.6`). ##### Minimal image, `minimal` tag. The minimal image is a stripped-down image that uses the **`microdnf`**⁠ as package manager which uses `libdnf` and hence doesn't require Python. This image is `52%` smaller in size (`37MB` download, `102MB` expanded), contains a very limited package set. The `almalinux:minimal` tag always points to the most recent version of the minimal image. `almalinux:8-minimal`) and minor (e.g. `almalinux:8.4-minimal`) releases are also available. This minimal image has an additional tag `almalinux/8-minimal`, its a mirror of `almalinux:minimal`, created to be consistent with other `UBI` variants. So, `docker pull almalinux/8-minimal` image is same as `docker pull almalinux:minimal`. ##### Base image, `almalinux/8-base` tag. The AlmaLinux Base Image is designed to be a base for your containerized applications, middleware and utilities. Base Image includes some helpful OS tools like find, tar, vi, etc., and a full DNF stack. The Image has some differences in a package set than the default(platform) image. docker pull almalinux/8-base. ##### Init image, `almalinux/8-init` tag. The AlmaLinux init image extends base image, designed to run an init system as PID 1 for running multi-services inside a container. docker pull almalinux/8-init. ##### Micro image, `almalinux/8-micro` tag. The AlmaLinux micro image is a stripped down image, distributed without any package manager. Micro image is `82%` smaller then `base` image, `68%` smaller then `minimal` image in size (`13MB` download, `36MB` expanded). docker pull almalinux/8-micro. View license information⁠ for the software contained in this image. docker pull almalinux/8-base:8.10-20251124.
